1.finding: 22:1 bonus (allotted 27-May-2026) and 1:2 split (4-May-2026) are applied to every year: EPS 5.64 / 1.42 / 0.57 and NAV 12.75 use the 55,650,984-share count. FY26 EPS divides PAT by the year-end count rather than a time-weighted count (the 9.65 m consideration shares were issued 22-Oct-2025); a weighted count would give a higher EPS, so the reported P/E is not flattered.

2.finding: CFO Rs 26.85 m in FY26 against PAT Rs 313.90 m (8.6%); cumulative CFO/PAT FY24-26 is 69.7% (281.93 / 404.39). FY26 absorbed a Rs 445.46 m inventory build (finished goods Rs 432.33 m vs Rs 19.26 m) and Rs 281.35 m other assets. Acquired balances came in through the slump sale, so the FY26 cash flow is not like-for-like with FY25.

3.finding: Current tax Rs 130.30 m on PBT Rs 444.12 m = 29.3% in FY26; cumulative FY24-26 current tax 147.09 / PBT 562.64 = 26.1%, above the 25.17% statutory rate. Deferred tax is negligible (credit Rs 0.09 m).

4.finding: Capex of Rs 716.64 m is to be built on 16.20 acres leased from the promoter Jagatjit Singh at Rs 0.08 m a month (+15% every 3 years, to 2055). Related-party purchases FY26 Rs 164.91 m (6.5% of materials consumed) from Goodfield, Expert International, A.P.U Traders and G9 International, each owned by persons with KMP influence. Loans/advances to promoters Rs 55.00 m outstanding at 31-Mar-2026. No proceeds go to a subsidiary.

5.finding: Fresh issue is amount-based (up to Rs 3,000 m), so there is no fixed share count and no objects price floor. Identified objects are Rs 2,001.64 m (66.7% of the fresh issue): working capital 1,100.00, Dehlon capex 716.64, debt repayment 185.00. The rest is offer expenses and general corporate purposes (up to 25% of gross proceeds, p. 124).

6.finding: No revaluation reserve in the restated balance sheet.

7.finding: Goodwill Rs 4.55 m = 0.6% of equity. The slump-sale businesses were taken in at carrying values (net assets Rs 320.03 m for consideration Rs 324.57 m; goodwill Rs 4.55 m). The proforma balance sheet shows goodwill of Rs 65.66 m (p. 91) against Rs 4.55 m in the restated one: the two treatments differ.

8.finding: Demand side: Seth Agro Industries 25.21% of FY26 revenue (Rs 1,043.46 m; 17.20% FY25, 3.85% FY24); top 10 customers 50.04%; no long-term agreements. Supply side improved: top supplier 7.94% and top 10 40.53% of FY26 purchases (76.68% FY25). Geography: Northern 68.04% and Central 25.95% of FY26 revenue.

9.finding: Contingent liabilities Rs 71.70 m (GST Rs 22.67 m, income tax Rs 0.18 m, other Rs 6.50 m, bank guarantees Rs 42.35 m) = 10.1% of net worth. Litigation: 8 tax proceedings and 1 regulatory matter against the company, Rs 27.71 m in aggregate; 2 criminal and 1 civil matter by the company, Rs 14.56 m.

R1.finding: Anup Kumar Jain & Co (FRN 005731N); no qualification or emphasis of matter in the restated report. Auditor history: Singla Gupta resigned 23-Apr-2024 (preoccupation), Kansal Sandeep & Associates filled the vacancy 2-May-2024 and ceased 30-Sep-2024 (tenure), Anup Kumar Jain appointed 30-Sep-2024 (p. 98). FY24 and FY25 are special-purpose Ind AS statements; the earlier statutory auditor did not hold a peer-review certificate and did not perform the restatement (p. 343).

R2.finding: The parent's accounting software recorded an audit trail (edit log) only from January 2026; before that it had no such feature (Note 52(xxi)). Audit-trail-at-database-level is also flagged as a risk (p. 52). The Rule 11(g) requirement is therefore met for part of FY26 only.

R3.finding: The company states it will appoint a monitoring agency before the RHP; issue size above Rs 500 m requires one. Not yet named.

R4.finding: Offer is under Reg 6(2) because Reg 6(1)(a) (net tangible assets Rs 30 m in each of three years) and 6(1)(c) (net worth Rs 10 m in each year) are not met: FY24 net worth was Rs 5.32 m (p. 85). At least 75% must be allotted to QIBs or the offer fails.

R6.finding: Keynote Financial Services has two IPOs in FY2026-27 (Rs 5,858 m) and none in FY2024-26 per the DRHP; both traded below issue at day 30 (-23.53% and -2.75%). Short record; see Appendix B.

R7.finding: Means of finance not separately tested at DRHP stage.

rationale.g1: FY26 revenue Rs 4,139.70 m is +63.1% on proforma FY25 Rs 2,537.60 m; proforma FY25 was +22.3% on FY24 (p. 92). The CARE report puts the domestic implements industry at 10.2% CAGR FY23-26 and farm equipment at 7.7% CAGR FY26-30 (pp. 248, 250). Bear is near the industry rate; Neutral fades from 25%; Bull holds above 30% for two years as Dehlon capacity (Mar-2028) arrives. Subsidy-driven demand (CRM and SMAM schemes, p. 56) can swing a year either way.
rationale.m: Proforma EBITDA margin 9.74% / 14.51% and restated FY26 13.46% (p. 158); three-year average 12.6%. Neutral uses the through-cycle 12.5%. The listed tractor peers run 13.2-13.3% (p. 161). Gross margin (23.6% to 39.1%) is not used: it moves with how labour and job-work are classified between materials and employee cost.
rationale.nwc: Trade NWC (inventory + receivables - trade payables) is 18.5% / 20.5% / 20.3% of revenue FY24-26 (proforma FY24-25, restated FY26; pp. 85, 91). Closing inventory days were about 165 against the issuer's 132 average-based days (p. 133). Neutral 20%; Bear 23%; Bull 18% as the issuer targets 130 inventory days and 45 receivable days.
rationale.roic: Issuer ROCE 31.1% FY26 and 31.6% proforma FY25 (p. 158) but the capital base is small and FY24 net worth was Rs 5.32 m. Neutral terminal ROIC 20%, above the cost of capital but well under the reported ROCE; Bear 13% near the cost of capital.
